title: Repeated administrative referrals
construct: Resolve legal and factual bottlenecks without displacing the responsible decision-maker. Each applicant has already received at least one forwarding order.

cases.title: Widow's pension
cases.record: The pension board accepts qualifying service but says Treasury holds the beneficiary match. Treasury says the board must first sanction payment.
cases.decision: Decide how responsibility for sanction and payment should be allocated.

cases.title: Wheelchair grant
cases.record: The equipment office approved eligibility but the district office questions whether the quoted wheelchair fits the grant. A second assessment would require travel.
cases.decision: Decide who should resolve specification and how to preserve the applicant's access.

cases.title: Crop relief
cases.record: An inspection lists the tenant's crop damage under the owner's account. Both filed claims and neither has been heard together.
cases.decision: Define the issue for a decision without prejudging the competing claim.

cases.title: Wage arrears
cases.record: The department admits attendance but says the contractor paid cash. The contractor filed an unsigned payment sheet.
cases.decision: Decide which part of the payment dispute can be resolved and by whom.

cases.title: Student stipend
cases.record: A district clerk accepted the application before closing day. A server timestamp shows central receipt one day late. Both offices refer to the other date.
cases.decision: Identify the effective date issue and the evidence needed to decide it.

cases.title: Food card transfer
cases.record: Both districts accept residency evidence. Each database marks the household active in the other district; the household has collected no grain for two months.
cases.decision: Decide whether a registry correction or a fresh entitlement determination is required.

cases.title: Flood rebuilding grant
cases.record: A field survey approved rebuilding, but the planning map puts the plot in a restricted zone. The families affected received the same referral letter.
cases.decision: Separate common mapping questions from individual entitlement.

cases.title: Reimbursement of treatment
cases.record: The fund accepts the hospital bill but disputes preauthorisation. The hospital says its own portal was down on admission day.
cases.decision: Decide how to obtain the outage evidence without making the patient chase both institutions.

cases.title: Apprentice certificate
cases.record: The training centre accepts completion, but the issuing office doubts the supervisor's authority. The applicant loses a job offer next week.
cases.decision: Decide whether an interim verification or a final direction is supportable.

cases.title: Freight permit refund
cases.record: The licensing officer admits duplicate collection but reports an old government debt. The debt unit cannot locate a signed demand.
cases.decision: Define which amount is conceded and what hearing is needed on set-off.

developments: A newly produced delegation names one officer with power to issue the underlying decision. Both agencies accept the document.
A dated receipt identifies a third person whose existing benefit or priority would change if the claim were granted in full.
The authority offers a signed, time-bound partial remedy that leaves the applicant's main contested ground undecided.
A fresh chronology suggests the applicant was expressly refused relief years earlier. They say service of that refusal went to the wrong address.
The responsible office concedes that its archive lost the only original. An independently held copy covers part of the disputed period.
tasks: Draft the enforceable operative paragraphs and specify when the applicant can return without filing a new claim.
Give a preliminary ruling identifying what can be decided now and the material still needed for the remainder.
Address the strongest reason to terminate the proceeding today and the strongest reason to keep it under supervision.
Explain the order directly to the applicant, including who must act first and what happens if that person does nothing.

criteria.name: Competence and threshold
criteria.zero: Merely forwards the file.
criteria.one: Identifies a possible decision-maker without resolving its disputed responsibility.
criteria.two: Uses record facts to assign the right decision or specify how competence will be resolved.

criteria.name: Contrary material
criteria.zero: Treats an admission or objection as disposing of everything.
criteria.one: Flags the disputed point without addressing its effect.
criteria.two: Separates admitted and disputed issues, hearing affected interests before adverse findings.

criteria.name: Effective remedy
criteria.zero: Gives an indefinite direction to consider.
criteria.one: Sets a deadline without a communication or default mechanism.
criteria.two: Assigns the task, timing, communication and accessible response to default.

title: Independent scrutiny of arrest and remand
construct: Scrutinise the basis and purpose of coercive custody using the stated facts and available alternatives.

cases.title: Seized phone
cases.record: Police seek custody to recover messages from a phone already seized. The defence identifies a cloud account still under the suspect's control.
cases.decision: Decide what investigative step, if any, actually requires custody.

cases.title: Witness contact
cases.record: A complainant reports a call after arrest. The caller ID belongs to a relative and the accused has had no phone in detention.
cases.decision: Decide whether the contact can fairly support detention.

cases.title: Unidentified lookout
cases.record: Officers arrested a person matching a clothing description. CCTV excludes one suspect but gives no clear face; an identification exercise is proposed.
cases.decision: Assess the need for continued custody pending identification.

cases.title: Warehouse keys
cases.record: Police say tools are hidden in a locked depot. A landlord offers lawful access and says the accused returned the keys yesterday.
cases.decision: Distinguish a search requiring access from a request requiring custody.

cases.title: Interstate arrest
cases.record: The diary records an arrest at 07:00. A toll record and signed receipt suggest control began the previous evening.
cases.decision: Resolve which custody timeline needs checking before authorisation.

cases.title: Untranslated reasons
cases.record: A written notice of grounds bears a thumb mark. Counsel reports the accused cannot read that language; the officer says an interpreter explained it.
cases.decision: Decide whether and how communication of grounds was effective.

cases.title: Hospital ward
cases.record: Doctors report a stable condition but recommend observation. The officer offers a general assurance of medical care during interrogation.
cases.decision: Decide whether medical needs and investigative steps can be reconciled.

cases.title: Password request
cases.record: Officers say the suspect alone knows a password. An expert says the service provider can preserve the records pending legal process.
cases.decision: Examine the proposed purpose and alternatives without assuming an obligation to disclose.

cases.title: Second suspect
cases.record: Police rely on another accused's interview. A contemporaneous attendance record places this person elsewhere during part of the alleged episode.
cases.decision: Assess the individual basis and necessity of the request.

cases.title: Brief production
cases.record: Video audio failed during private consultation. The officer says the accused previously waived counsel by a nod recorded in the station diary.
cases.decision: Decide whether a meaningful remand hearing can proceed now.

developments: A contemporaneous log conflicts with a material assertion in the officer's account. Its author is available to answer questions.
Duty counsel identifies a preservation step that can be taken without custody. The investigator disputes whether it covers one remaining lead.
The accused reports an injury incurred after arrest. No private medical assessment has yet been offered.
An interpreter confirms that one substantive part of the earlier explanation was omitted; the parties disagree about the legal consequence.
The officer withdraws the stock allegations and relies on a single new, time-sensitive fact that defence counsel has not seen.
tasks: State the questions you would put to both sides before deciding custody and how the answers could alter your decision.
Dictate a reasoned custody disposition with immediate directions and a time for review if appropriate.
Explain what can fairly proceed on this record and what requires verification before liberty can be restricted.
Respond to the strongest submission against your proposed disposition, including a concrete less restrictive alternative.

criteria.name: Individual scrutiny
criteria.zero: Accepts the request by formula.
criteria.one: Identifies a disputed assertion without testing it.
criteria.two: Tests purpose, chronology and individual evidence before deciding necessity.

criteria.name: Hearing and safeguards
criteria.zero: Orders custody over an unresolved impediment to participation.
criteria.one: Mentions safeguards but gives no remedial step.
criteria.two: Secures meaningful participation and addresses the new defect or contested evidence.

criteria.name: Limits and alternatives
criteria.zero: Gives indefinite or unexplained coercive relief.
criteria.one: Offers an alternative disconnected from the stated risk.
criteria.two: Connects a bounded direction to the actual risk and explains the availability or insufficiency of alternatives.

title: Framing charges on individual evidence
construct: Apply the stipulated screening task: identify material capable of connecting this accused with the alleged conduct while reserving final credibility findings for trial.

cases.title: Circulation list
cases.record: A procurement officer's name appears on a distribution list. The approval bears another officer's signature. An email shows the accused asked for a price revision.
cases.decision: Decide whether the file connects the accused to the alleged collusion.

cases.title: Vehicle custody
cases.record: A van used in a theft is registered to the accused. A lease says it was let to a driver, but a toll payment came from the owner's card.
cases.decision: Evaluate the link to participation rather than ownership alone.

cases.title: Altered invoice
cases.record: The accused edited a spreadsheet. The audit history shows the edit changed a date, while a different login changed the amount.
cases.decision: Separate proof of access from proof of the charged alteration.

cases.title: Shared locker
cases.record: Cash was found in a locker accessible to three staff. One message from the accused asks a colleague to clear the shelf before audit.
cases.decision: Assess the link between the message and the alleged concealment.

cases.title: Diverted medicines
cases.record: Shortages occurred during the accused's shift. A signed dispatch note records a transfer to another ward without a receipt.
cases.decision: Determine whether the record supports diversion by this accused.

cases.title: Street identification
cases.record: A witness first described a taller person and later recognised the accused in a photo. A transit record places the accused near the scene.
cases.decision: Identify whether the evidentiary conflict needs trial or leaves the link missing.

cases.title: Trust funds
cases.record: A trustee challenged a transfer in the minutes. A later authorisation bears their initials but lacks a date.
cases.decision: Assess what the documents can support about assent.

cases.title: Counterfeit permit
cases.record: The applicant submitted a false permit and produced a receipt from a broker. A warning email went to a shared inbox.
cases.decision: Assess the material on knowledge without determining final guilt.

cases.title: Unlawful gathering
cases.record: A video shows the accused arriving as damage ends. A witness describes giving directions earlier but does not identify the words.
cases.decision: Decide whether individual participation is supported.

cases.title: Data export
cases.record: An access log identifies a workstation, not its user. The accused had booked it but the roster shows a colleague worked late.
cases.decision: Explain what connects the login to the person charged.

developments: A document relied on as independent corroboration comes from the same source as the principal allegation.
The prosecution accepts that one time stamp is wrong and supplies a corrected sequence open to two interpretations.
The defence identifies an account consistent with the undisputed record but dependent on a witness whose credibility is contested.
The only reference said to identify the accused is an abbreviation shared with another person. Other circumstantial material remains.
A party invites the court to apply an inference drawn against a co-accused whose duties and access were materially different.
tasks: Draft the threshold ruling, identifying the strongest link and the weakest necessary link.
State what remains for trial and what the court must actually decide at screening.
Explain why the rival account does or does not undermine the required individual link at this stage.
Address both sides on one inference that would turn this screening into a premature finding of guilt.

criteria.name: Individual nexus
criteria.zero: Substitutes title, association or accusation for a link.
criteria.one: Names evidence without tracing it to conduct and person.
criteria.two: Connects specific material to the necessary conduct and explains any missing link.

criteria.name: Treatment of conflict
criteria.zero: Ignores conflicting evidence or finally decides credibility.
criteria.one: Mentions rival material without weighing its relevance at this stage.
criteria.two: Explains what the conflict changes under the stipulated threshold and what remains for trial.

criteria.name: Operative reasoning
criteria.zero: Copies the prosecution conclusion.
criteria.one: Gives an outcome with generic threshold language.
criteria.two: States the decision, the stage-specific reason and the unresolved issue.

title: Legislator-advocate conflicts
construct: In the exercise, elected status alone does not disqualify counsel. Investigate case-specific overlap and protect client representation and fair process.

cases.title: Road concession
cases.record: An MLA acting for a bidder voted for a roads budget and chaired a confidential hearing about this tender. The hearing transcript is sealed.
cases.decision: Determine what overlap matters for today's interim hearing.

cases.title: School closure
cases.record: An MP represents parents and publicly criticised the policy. A minister says the MP privately received the school inspection notes.
cases.decision: Separate political speech from access to disputed evidence.

cases.title: Compensation table
cases.record: An MLA acting for claimants signed a committee report annexing the table now challenged. The client relies on a later public version.
cases.decision: Decide whether the versions and counsel's earlier involvement create an evidentiary conflict.

cases.title: Hospital audit
cases.record: Counsel questioned an auditor in committee and now appears for the hospital against that auditor's findings. A junior can argue on public material.
cases.decision: Manage the cross-examination and representation problem.

cases.title: Land acquisition
cases.record: An MLA appeared as counsel before learning a constituent's complaint they forwarded is now an exhibit. The receipt bears counsel's annotations.
cases.decision: Assess possible witness status without imputing wrongdoing.

cases.title: Election printing
cases.record: The MP advised a printer oversight group. The disputed correction log was never tabled; the opponent says the MP saw it privately.
cases.decision: Decide how to handle a contested claim of special access.

cases.title: Flood procurement
cases.record: An MLA asked for supplier names on the House floor. The names are public but an unpublished pricing schedule is disputed.
cases.decision: Identify which information requires protection.

cases.title: Energy tariff
cases.record: An elected advocate disclosed a client retainer after participating in a legislative hearing about the same tariff. The precise dates conflict.
cases.decision: Plan an impartial chronology inquiry.

cases.title: Committee privilege
cases.record: Counsel's client relies on a document counsel says was received in open correspondence. An opponent says it was confidential committee evidence.
cases.decision: Decide how to test provenance without indiscriminate compelled disclosure.

cases.title: Constituency grant
cases.record: An MLA appears against a trust whose grant the MLA recommended. The legal claim concerns accounts made after the recommendation.
cases.decision: Examine the temporal and substantive overlap before ruling.

developments: Junior counsel is ready on the public record. A disputed confidential document would be essential only to one prayer.
A verified chronology shows the political role began after most disputed events but before one material review meeting.
A witness asserts personal contact with counsel on the disputed transaction and offers dated correspondence not yet disclosed to the client.
The opponent concedes that most allegedly privileged facts were already public. One source remains disputed.
Immediate exclusion would cause the client to miss an irreversible deadline. Opposing counsel offers a temporary standstill on defined terms.
tasks: Issue directions for a conflict hearing that preserve privilege and both parties' opportunity to answer.
Decide whether today's hearing can proceed, with whom and on which material.
Explain the difference between an appearance concern, possible witness status and proved professional misconduct in this file.
Address an application for immediate exclusion and identify a proportionate alternative or why it fails.

criteria.name: Factual conflict
criteria.zero: Treats office or party as decisive.
criteria.one: Identifies an overlap without examining its materiality.
criteria.two: Tests personal involvement, chronology and information relevant to this proceeding.

criteria.name: Fair process
criteria.zero: Finds misconduct or orders blanket disclosure without hearing parties.
criteria.one: Seeks disclosure without protecting legitimate confidences.
criteria.two: Defines a narrow inquiry, gives an opportunity to answer and reserves contested disciplinary findings.

criteria.name: Client and adversary protection
criteria.zero: Lets the deadline or exclusion decide the merits by default.
criteria.one: Offers an accommodation without addressing the opposing risk.
criteria.two: Orders a feasible interim arrangement and explains protection for both sides.

title: Urgent listing and political influence
construct: One contested hearing slot remains today. The next regular listing is tomorrow. Apply the same urgency criteria to each request.

cases.title: Rally and eviction
cases.record: A candidate challenges a loudspeaker condition before a rally; a family faces eviction at dawn. The family has a disputed stay receipt.
cases.decision: Select a hearing and address the other deadline.

cases.title: Counting and medicines
cases.record: A candidate seeks preservation of counting footage due for overwrite. A clinic seeks access to medicines for tonight.
cases.decision: Determine which loss can be prevented without a full merits hearing.

cases.title: Press event and custody
cases.record: A minister seeks relief over a publication before an evening press event. A legal-aid client remains in custody despite an apparent release order.
cases.decision: Compare timing, harm and available communication routes.

cases.title: Ballot correction and wages
cases.record: The ballot locks tonight. Workers say a withdrawing contractor will remove the only payroll records overnight.
cases.decision: Identify which interest requires the contested slot.

cases.title: Security detail and shelter
cases.record: An elected member challenges withdrawal of escorts citing a threat letter. A shelter faces closure before a storm.
cases.decision: Decide what verification permits safe triage today.

cases.title: Campaign sign and examinations
cases.record: A party seeks restoration of signs before voting; students need admission cards before morning exams. Both respondents contest entitlement.
cases.decision: Rank requests and consider interim access for the deferred applicant.

cases.title: Broadcast and dialysis
cases.record: A public debate excludes a candidate. A patient faces a cancelled early-morning dialysis slot after a reimbursement dispute.
cases.decision: Assess irreversibility and alternatives for each applicant.

cases.title: Nomination and crop seizure
cases.record: A contested nomination closes today. A grower says seized produce will perish before the next hearing.
cases.decision: Design an order that addresses practical loss in both files.

cases.title: Committee disclosure and wages
cases.record: An MP seeks an unredacted report before a vote. A worker asks to freeze a transfer allegedly designed to defeat an existing award.
cases.decision: Assess available partial disclosures and preservation steps.

cases.title: Audit publication and demolition
cases.record: A party seeks an urgent answer to an audit report before polling. A municipality says an unstable structure must be demolished at first light despite an occupant's challenge.
cases.decision: Determine what evidence is needed immediately in both cases.

developments: The respondent in the first matter offers an enforceable standstill until noon tomorrow, limited to the identified applicant.
An independent record contradicts the second applicant's stated deadline, although the substantive harm remains disputed.
The respondent in the second matter cannot take an irreversible step without a second official's signature, and the official is available now.
A new exhibit materially strengthens the first applicant's urgency claim. The other side needs ten minutes to authenticate it.
Both applicants identify interim measures. Only one has the necessary affected party present to agree binding terms.
tasks: Give both registry entries with times, responsibilities and the basis for any temporary protection.
Explain to the deferred applicant exactly what could bring the matter back before the deadline.
Identify the fact most likely to reverse the ranking and give a provisional allocation on the present record.
Decide whether to use the slot for contested relief or obtain limited undertakings and explain the consequences for each applicant.

criteria.name: Comparable harm
criteria.zero: Prioritises office, wealth or popularity by itself.
criteria.one: Lists deadlines without comparing reversibility.
criteria.two: Uses one urgency test and compares deadline, severity and available protection in both matters.

criteria.name: Usable protection
criteria.zero: Defers a case without addressing irreversible harm.
criteria.one: Suggests an undertaking without verifying authority or scope.
criteria.two: Defines feasible protection or explains its absence, identifying who is bound and until when.

criteria.name: Reviewable allocation
criteria.zero: Promises time the court does not have.
criteria.one: Chooses a slot with general reasons.
criteria.two: Produces a feasible clock, records the decisive fact and provides a return route.

title: Public interest litigation and abusive process
construct: Screen public injury, standing, evidence and proportionality without allowing motive alone to resolve disputed facts.

cases.title: River sampling
cases.record: A rival contractor challenges pollution using lab results from a competitor's outfall. Chain of custody covers only one sample.
cases.decision: Decide which allegations warrant verification.

cases.title: Clinic closures
cases.record: An opposition organiser cites six clinic closures. District records show two reopened; attendance logs for the other four are missing.
cases.decision: Choose the scope of any public inquiry.

cases.title: Unsafe hostels
cases.record: A student organisation files anonymous photographs of blocked exits. Building plans identify two corridors but not the date of the images.
cases.decision: Decide how to verify a safety risk without exposing residents.

cases.title: Land tender
cases.record: A losing bidder claims public loss from an auction and omits an earlier commercial challenge. A valuation discrepancy is documented.
cases.decision: Separate private redress from a credible public issue.

cases.title: Voting access
cases.record: A volunteer alleges polling booths are inaccessible using photos from earlier elections. Current access maps disagree about three locations.
cases.decision: Specify fast verification ahead of polling.

cases.title: Drinking water
cases.record: A campaigning councillor challenges supply contamination. An accredited test supports one neighbourhood but not the entire district claimed.
cases.decision: Decide what relief the geographic evidence supports.

cases.title: Shelter roll
cases.record: An NGO alleges ghost residents and seeks publication of names. Receipts suggest a duplicate claim; residents fear identification.
cases.decision: Review the evidence without creating new exposure.

cases.title: School meals
cases.record: A political rival alleges ration diversion using purchase orders but no distribution records. Parents offer direct testimony.
cases.decision: Identify what should be heard before ordering a general audit.

cases.title: Street lighting
cases.record: A former supplier alleges inflated billing in every ward. Meter logs support a discrepancy in one ward and fail to cover three others.
cases.decision: Decide whether the inquiry should extend citywide.

cases.title: Prison letters
cases.record: A media campaign reproduces unsigned letters alleging denial of medical visits. One dated referral is independently corroborated.
cases.decision: Order an appropriate preliminary response without deciding systemic guilt.

developments: The petitioner discloses an undisclosed financial backer with a direct interest. One independent source still supports a public injury.
A district authority offers raw records to the court but insists affected people must remain unidentified.
A separate proceeding concerns the same project but seeks only personal compensation.
A named source retracts one assertion under circumstances that remain uncertain. Documentary material supports a narrower claim.
The government concedes the reported anomaly in one location and submits an action plan with no completion date.
tasks: Give a threshold decision on the scope of the case and what must be verified before escalation.
Decide whether a change of petitioner, independent assistance or dismissal would serve affected people on this record.
Dictate a proportionate interim inquiry with responsible parties and confidentiality arrangements.
Respond to an application for costs alleging political abuse while preserving any independently substantiated issue.

criteria.name: Interest and standing
criteria.zero: Treats political motive as proof of abuse or innocence.
criteria.one: Notes the interest without relating it to the claim.
criteria.two: Separates private incentives from independently supported public injury.

criteria.name: Evidence and scope
criteria.zero: Orders a roving inquiry or rejects all material unread.
criteria.one: Names evidence but leaves scope undefined.
criteria.two: Matches scrutiny and provisional findings to verified material and conflicting accounts.

criteria.name: Proportionate procedure
criteria.zero: Punishes or grants broad relief without a hearing.
criteria.one: Proposes scrutiny without a bounded mechanism.
criteria.two: Chooses a defined procedure, protects affected people and gives reasons and review conditions.

title: Poverty, custody and meaningful bail
construct: A release order exists but the applicant remains in custody. Test whether the condition blocking release serves a demonstrated risk and whether a workable substitute exists.

cases.title: Local surety
cases.record: A migrant worker cannot find a local property owner. A prior missed hearing occurred after notice went to a previous address.
cases.decision: Address attendance without imposing an impossible condition.

cases.title: Cash deposit
cases.record: A domestic worker cannot pay the deposit. The prosecutor points to travel to another district for work and one voluntary return.
cases.decision: Assess the actual flight risk and practicable assurance.

cases.title: Digital reporting
cases.record: A person cannot register weekly through a smartphone application from a village without coverage. A nearby police post keeps a paper register.
cases.decision: Decide whether alternative reporting meets the purpose.

cases.title: Address proof
cases.record: A pavement resident has no utility bill. A shelter will confirm contact but cannot guarantee long-term accommodation.
cases.decision: Design a means of contact without assuming a permanent address.

cases.title: Language barrier
cases.record: The release order requires an undertaking in a language the accused cannot read. The registry says a signature alone suffices.
cases.decision: Secure informed compliance and identify remaining release obstacles.

cases.title: Verification delay
cases.record: A surety is willing but title verification has taken six weeks. An official says a government database mismatch caused delay.
cases.decision: Decide whether alternative verification permits earlier release.

cases.title: Work hours
cases.record: Daily daytime reporting would cost a factory worker their job. The prosecutor raises one documented attempt to contact a witness.
cases.decision: Separate attendance conditions from witness protection.

cases.title: Travel restriction
cases.record: An arrested caregiver must cross the district border for treatment. A past address change was unreported during a hospital stay.
cases.decision: Balance contactability and access to care.

cases.title: Multiple orders
cases.record: Bail has been granted in two cases with inconsistent reporting locations. Neither court was told of the other condition.
cases.decision: Identify which body can change which obligation and how release can occur.

cases.title: Transport cost
cases.record: A weekly long-distance appearance costs more than a day’s earnings. A prior failure coincided with cancelled transport but no receipt survives.
cases.decision: Test the reliability of the attendance concern and a lower-cost plan.

developments: An independent contact offers verifiable notice delivery but refuses to assume an unlimited financial obligation.
The prosecution discloses a documented past breach. The applicant offers a specific explanation supported only in part.
Jail staff confirm that changing the disputed condition alone would still leave a separate administrative hold requiring verification.
An available local official can monitor a narrower condition and report noncompliance within one working day.
A proposed substitute would shift a substantial recurring expense onto an equally poor relative.
tasks: Give a reasoned disposition and a release communication plan naming the person who verifies execution.
Explain which risk the original condition served and whether the proposed substitute addresses that risk.
Describe the immediate inquiry and a fallback if the first substitute proves infeasible today.
Address the prosecutor's strongest objection and the cost to the applicant of maintaining the present condition.

criteria.name: Individual risk
criteria.zero: Treats poverty as flight risk or ignores a documented concern.
criteria.one: Names a risk without testing its factual basis.
criteria.two: Distinguishes financial inability, notice failure and demonstrated noncompliance on the record.

criteria.name: Feasible conditions
criteria.zero: Repeats the barrier or assumes another person can pay.
criteria.one: Suggests an alternative without checking its practical operation.
criteria.two: Chooses a legally available, workable option or gives reasons for retaining a condition in light of alternatives.

criteria.name: Actual release
criteria.zero: Assumes a paper order ensures release.
criteria.one: Directs communication without follow-up.
criteria.two: Identifies the recipient, verification time and a response to continued detention or another hold.

title: Judicial insults and repair
construct: You made an inaccurate personal remark in open court. Repair the hearing, the record and the practical harm under the stated circumstances.

cases.title: Repeat filing
cases.record: You called the applicant a professional nuisance and dismissed a supposed duplicate. The new application challenges a later notice.
cases.decision: Repair both the remark and the lost hearing.

cases.title: Missing translation
cases.record: You mocked a witness for changing an answer. An interpreter reports the first question was mistranslated and the witness is now silent.
cases.decision: Preserve reliable evidence and restore an opportunity to answer.

cases.title: Legal-aid papers
cases.record: You described legal-aid counsel as unprepared. The registry confirms it served an incomplete brief and costs are under consideration.
cases.decision: Correct the attribution and decide how to hear the client fairly.

cases.title: Medical absence
cases.record: You likened a litigant's illness explanation to theatre. Hospital records confirm admission but do not establish the entire absence claimed.
cases.decision: Withdraw the insult while addressing the remaining procedural issue.

cases.title: Remote disconnection
cases.record: You accused a remote applicant of staging a dropout. The court log shows a server outage, although other delays remain unexplained.
cases.decision: Restore participation and decide what can proceed today.

cases.title: Bank account mismatch
cases.record: You called the applicant a fraudster because two account names differ. An identity update explains the spelling but one transfer is disputed.
cases.decision: Separate correction from unresolved merits.

cases.title: Witness expense
cases.record: You called a witness greedy for seeking travel costs. The summons required attendance from another district, and the applicable rate is disputed.
cases.decision: Correct the remark and make a fair expense decision.

cases.title: Clothing remark
cases.record: You mocked how a self-represented litigant was dressed. The other side then described the litigant as unreliable. Their documents remain disputed.
cases.decision: Repair the evidentiary and interpersonal effect of your words.

cases.title: Injury evidence
cases.record: You ridiculed a photograph as staged. The original has independent metadata but the cause of injury remains contested.
cases.decision: Reopen the factual issue without prejudging it in the opposite direction.

cases.title: Clerical mix-up
cases.record: You publicly reprimanded a junior lawyer for an altered exhibit. The registry now identifies its own scanning error. The opposing party relied on the incorrect copy.
cases.decision: Correct the record and protect both parties' hearing rights.

developments: The affected person asks to give their response in writing and declines a direct apology meeting.
A public report accurately quotes your remark. The affected person wants the correction to be equally accessible.
The party asks for reassignment. Another bench can hear the matter today if the file is transferred promptly.
One party proposes erasing the original exchange from the public record; the affected person asks for an appended correction.
A time-sensitive interim loss will occur while the remark is being addressed. The opponent offers a brief standstill if its terms are recorded.
tasks: Speak the next four sentences in open court and specify the procedural direction that follows.
Draft the correction and distinguish the finding that must be withdrawn from any still-open merits issue.
Decide whether to continue the hearing, pause or seek reassignment, accounting for the practical deadline.
Explain to the affected person how they can be heard and how they will know the corrected decision reached the proper recipients.

criteria.name: Personal accountability
criteria.zero: Defends the insult or blames the recipient.
criteria.one: Expresses general regret without correcting the material error.
criteria.two: Identifies and withdraws the exact wrong, addresses the person and corrects the relevant record.

criteria.name: Effective hearing
criteria.zero: Demands forgiveness or treats silence as assent.
criteria.one: Offers a hearing without making it usable.
criteria.two: Restores a meaningful response channel and resolves the procedural consequence without conditioning it on forgiveness.

criteria.name: Independent merits
criteria.zero: Uses a favourable outcome as a substitute for repair or leaves the prejudice intact.
criteria.one: Notes a remaining issue without a fair plan.
criteria.two: Separates corrected facts from contested issues and specifies a fair decision-maker or next hearing step.

title: Court reporting, confidentiality and open justice
construct: Address a requested restriction on reporting of an open hearing. Consider reliable attribution, concrete harm and less restrictive measures.

cases.title: Oral observation
cases.record: A headline treats a judge's question as a finding. The article body correctly describes the exchange. Counsel seeks a reporting ban.
cases.decision: Identify the precise error and proportionate response.

cases.title: Quoted affidavit
cases.record: A clip shows the judge repeating an accusation from an affidavit. Its introduction was removed. A party demands contempt action.
cases.decision: Verify attribution and the effect of editing.

cases.title: Protected identity
cases.record: An accurate article indirectly identifies a protected participant through employer and village. Counsel seeks removal of the full article.
cases.decision: Define the information that creates the risk and possible redaction.

cases.title: Embargo confusion
cases.record: A reporter published a draft order circulated by mistake. The signed version changes one operative paragraph.
cases.decision: Correct the public account and consider any justified restriction.

cases.title: Court sketch
cases.record: A sketch identifies a disputed witness in an otherwise open hearing. The witness reports threats but provides no verified source.
cases.decision: Evaluate risk without assuming every depiction is harmful.

cases.title: Medical exhibit
cases.record: A broadcast describes an intimate diagnosis visible briefly on a public screen. Its relevance to the dispute is limited.
cases.decision: Decide whether access arrangements or reporting limits are justified.

cases.title: Misleading translation
cases.record: Two translations of an oral direction differ on whether payment was mandatory. The signed order uses different language again.
cases.decision: Clarify the operative position before considering sanctions.

cases.title: Remote participant
cases.record: A livestream reveals an address on a document held to camera. Counsel seeks to close all further hearings.
cases.decision: Address the exposed detail and prevent recurrence.

cases.title: Source attribution
cases.record: A report quotes opposing counsel but a social post attributes the words to the judge. The publisher offers a correction.
cases.decision: Determine who can correct which account and what the court should record.

cases.title: Parallel proceedings
cases.record: A party alleges that reporting a preliminary statement will influence another hearing. The report accurately identifies the procedural stage.
cases.decision: Examine the specific risk and available narrower safeguards.

developments: The reporter offers a prompt, prominently placed clarification without altering accurate underlying material.
An affected nonparty identifies a specific safety risk and seeks confidential verification before any public ruling.
The full authorised recording resolves attribution of the words but does not resolve whether publication caused the alleged harm.
A blanket restriction would also cover an unrelated public-interest issue due to be heard tomorrow.
A narrower time-limited order could protect one identifiable detail. Existing copies are already circulating elsewhere.
tasks: Draft the proposed disposition including subject matter, duration, affected parties and opportunity for review where relevant.
Give an immediate verification plan and say what, if anything, can be done pending verification.
Explain the difference between correcting the record and restricting another person's reporting on these facts.
Respond to the strongest case for a blanket restraint and test a specific narrower measure.

criteria.name: Verification
criteria.zero: Sanctions or restricts on a cropped or disputed account alone.
criteria.one: Mentions verification without specifying the record or affected parties.
criteria.two: Checks the authoritative record, attribution and actual risk with an opportunity to answer.

criteria.name: Open justice and harm
criteria.zero: Treats embarrassment or public curiosity as decisive.
criteria.one: Mentions competing interests generically.
criteria.two: Weighs the specific injury and the speech or access displaced by the proposed order.

criteria.name: Narrow remedy
criteria.zero: Imposes an indefinite blanket restraint or ignores a concrete risk.
criteria.one: Suggests a narrower measure without scope or review.
criteria.two: Defines an effective proportionate step and explains its limits, duration and review.

title: Faith, adult autonomy and alleged restraint
construct: An adult’s voluntary choices and present freedom are contested. The exercise gives the court authority to examine alleged restraint, with any investigation of past wrongdoing handled separately.

cases.title: Study centre
cases.record: An adult chose to study at a centre but privately asked a friend for an exit key. The centre says it keeps keys for safety.
cases.decision: Examine present ability to leave and the person’s chosen destination.

cases.title: Family supervision
cases.record: Parents say their adult child consented to remain at home after changing faith. The adult answers only in a relative's presence.
cases.decision: Create a reliable opportunity to speak freely.

cases.title: Marriage dispute
cases.record: An adult says the marriage was chosen freely. A spouse holds the passport and says it was handed over for safekeeping.
cases.decision: Separate choice of partner from access to identity documents.

cases.title: Ritual retreat
cases.record: An adult entered a silent retreat willingly. A request to leave is disputed because a written quiet-period agreement was signed.
cases.decision: Determine present consent without judging the belief.

cases.title: Housing dependency
cases.record: A family withdrew housing after an adult chose another faith. A host offers shelter only if the adult signs a belief statement.
cases.decision: Distinguish absence of safe options from freely chosen accommodation.

cases.title: Interpretation conflict
cases.record: An interpreter supplied by a spiritual group renders the adult's answer as consent. An independent listener says the original was ambiguous.
cases.decision: Decide how to verify the person's own words.

cases.title: Telephone control
cases.record: An adult's earlier texts describe a chosen course of study. Current calls are answered by a relative who says the phone is broken.
cases.decision: Plan a safe direct conversation and address access to communication.

cases.title: Police protection
cases.record: An adult requests protection from family threats but refuses an escorted return home. An officer says supervision is the safest solution.
cases.decision: Consider protection without imposing custody.

cases.title: Public disclosure
cases.record: An adult asks to withhold their address after leaving a community. A parent claims knowing the location is essential to verify safety.
cases.decision: Balance verification and confidentiality on the actual evidence.

cases.title: Competing messages
cases.record: Two voice notes give different accounts of an adult's wishes. One was recorded with relatives nearby; timestamps are disputed.
cases.decision: Establish present wishes independently and separate historic allegations.

developments: In private, the adult distinguishes an earlier voluntary decision from a changed present choice and asks for a different immediate arrangement.
The adult accepts help from an independent support person but declines contact with both groups appearing in court.
A disputed recording shows a possible threat last week. Its production increases concern about disclosing the adult's present location.
The proposed safe destination proves unavailable tonight. A neutral temporary option is offered, subject to the adult's consent.
An interested relative offers transport while demanding continuous location tracking. The adult objects to that condition.
tasks: Give the next hearing directions and explain how the adult can accept, decline or change the immediate plan.
Draft an operative order dealing separately with liberty today, privacy and any historic allegation.
State what evidence changes your assessment and identify one unresolved fact that does not justify delaying a voluntary departure.
Explain the limits of the court's authority to the competing parties and give an immediately workable protection plan.

criteria.name: Independent voice
criteria.zero: Accepts interested accounts as conclusive.
criteria.one: Asks for wishes without ensuring private, accessible communication.
criteria.two: Obtains and weighs an independent account, distinguishing prior from current consent.

criteria.name: Jurisdiction and evidence
criteria.zero: Chooses the person's faith, relationship or custodian without authority.
criteria.one: Recognises autonomy but lets historic uncertainty control present liberty.
criteria.two: Separates present restraint and protection from contested history and personal religious judgments.

criteria.name: Effective choice
criteria.zero: Orders compulsory supervision or discloses a location without addressing risk.
criteria.one: Offers generic protection without checking consent or feasibility.
criteria.two: Sets out a consensual, practical arrangement including the responsible person and proportionate privacy safeguards.
